newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish public debt up 16.8 pct at PLN 195 bln.
newsitem.headline: Polish public debt up 16.8 pct at PLN 195 bln.

text.p: Poland's public debt rose 16.8 percent this year to 195.29 billion zlotys and is seen at 217.05 billion at the end of 1997, Piotr Dziewulski, head of the finance ministry's public debt department, said on Friday.

Dziewulski told a news conference, however, the share of public debt in the gross domestic product (GDP) this year fell to 54.7 percent from 58.5 percent in 1995 and is expected to fall to 50.5 percent in 1997. @

He said that domestic debt amounted to 77.6 billion zlotys or 39.7 percent of the total and foreign debt was 117.7 billion zlotys or 60.3 percent. The domestic debt was composed in almost 93 percent of treasury papers.
The share of short-term debt fell in zloty terms by 743 million zlotys this year to 31.0 billion zlotys or 40.0 percent of domestic debt.
On the other hand the share of medium and long-term debt rose by 7.8 billion zlotys to 16.7 billion zlotys or 21.6 percent of the domestic debt. @
"The rising share of longer-term instruments allows better liquidity management, and is much safer from the point of view of the budget," Dziewulski said.
He said the government currently had no debts in the National Bank of Poland even though the limit of borrowing in the NBP this year was 6.2 billion zlotys.
"Next year the limit will be yet smaller at 2.55 billion zlotys, which, in fact is a technical reserve in case of extraordinary problems with getting financing elsewhere," Dziewulski said.
